title: Soft commitment escrow and hosted burst mitigation procedures
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a soft-commitment (escrow) mechanism for dedicated capacity and a coordinated hosted-burst mitigation procedure so that when dedicated pools approach exhaustion we can safely spill traffic to hosted with bounded customer experience regression and cost visibility. This ticket defines the contract, runtime signals, arbitration rules, and operator playbook for the feature.
background: We continue to observe short-lived tenant bursts that exhaust dedicated slots and cause either hard failures or uncontrolled spillover to hosted with poor cost transparency. Recent incident INC-2026-02 showed a spike where a tenant’s ephemeral burst caused a cascade of model demotions and SLA violations in hosted backfill. Current routing logic lacks an explicit soft-commitment phase that reserves an escrow of capacity and coordinates downstream fallbacks and telemetry for billing and SLOs.
proposed_solution: Introduce 'soft-commit' escrow tokens per tenant that hold a lightweight reservation against a dedicated pool for a configurable grace window (e.g., 30s-5m). When a request would exceed hard reserved capacity, the router attempts to spend escrow tokens: if available, route to dedicated with a conditional admission that can be preempted; if not available, evaluate hosted fallback paths based on tier, region, cost budget, and model variant compatibility. Add a policy layer that: 1) prioritizes tenants with escrow balance; 2) enforces per-tenant hosted spill budgets; 3) emits telemetry tying each spilled request to an escrow decision and reason code for billing & quality monitoring. Build runtime guards: circuit-breakers that demote to cheaper quantized variants before falling back to hosted, hysteresis to prevent flip-flopping, and a metered accounting stream so Finance/PM can attribute hosted costs to tenant events. Coordination: small state machine in the orchestrator + token bucket-like escrow store, with a best-effort replication to edge routers to minimize latency checks.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-commit escrow tokens implemented with configurable TTL and per-tenant limits
Router evaluates escrow then fallback path within 2ms median added latency
Hosted spill includes tags: tenant_id, escrow_consumed, reason_code, model_variant, route_latency
Billing pipeline receives hosted_spill events and attributes cost to tenant within 24h
Hysteresis prevents repeated flip-flop for same tenant for at least 60s after a spill
E2E tests simulate burst traffic showing reduced hard failures and controlled hosted cost growth <= 15% against baseline
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime feature flag (global) and per-tenant opt-in
Stage 1: Canary in internal staging region with 5 internal tenants (2 weeks)
Stage 2: Limited public beta for low-risk tenants with explicit billing consent (4 weeks)
Stage 3: Gradual ramp with telemetry thresholds, auto-disable if error rate > 3% or hosted cost surge > 40%
Full rollout after 2 successful cycles and stakeholder sign-off
testing_and_metrics: Load test with synthetic burst traffic (90th/95th/99th token/sec profiles) to validate escrow TTL and eviction
Latency delta and P50/P95 for routing decision (<2ms added; P95 <10ms)
Hosted spill rate per tenant and aggregated hosted cost attributed to spills
SLO impact: error_rate, p99 request latency, and model quality regression (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval prompts) for spilled-to-hosted responses
Chaos test: simulated network partition between orchestrator and edge to validate best-effort behavior and safe defaults
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Escrow token store becomes hot and increases read/write latency - Mitigation: local LRU cache with best-effort TTL and batched writes to central store
Risk: Mis-attribution of cost for hosted backfill - Mitigation: include unique escrow_trace_id in every spilled request and add reconciliation job in billing pipeline
Risk: Flip-flopping between dedicated/hosted causing model quality regressions - Mitigation: implement hysteresis and progressive demotion to cheaper variants before hosted fallback
Risk: Tenants abuse escrow to get sustained over-commit - Mitigation: per-tenant rate limits, adaptive escrow refill policies tied to historical usage and contract tier
